response_text: To set up and start a thread from the user’s perspective, you begin by initializing the kernel, which prepares any necessary data structures and internal variables the operating system needs. Next, you write a thread function that contains the code you want the thread to run. This function must follow the expected format, typically taking a void* parameter and returning nothing. After that, you create the thread by calling a kernel function that allocates a stack and sets up the thread’s context so it’s ready to run. Finally, you start the kernel, which begins executing the thread by switching to its stack and running the function you defined. If everything is set up correctly, the thread will begin executing, and you can observe its behavior, usually through printed output.\n
